What degraded

  • Shipped at the round cap at 6.948, 0.75 under round 3's 7.7 rung and 1.05 under the 8.0 bar. The craft floor stood down with the art median at 6.4.
  • Frame 7's drawer runs off the right edge on every version, so the 100 behind 'nearly 10 in 100' can't be counted in the picture. Queued as card-drawer-spacing-ignores-length.
  • Frame 5's wristbands still read as rings, frame 2's notched top card doesn't show, frames 4 and 8 sit in the mid tones, and frame 6's declared value cut never rendered darker than frame 3.
  • Slide 8 does not say the May preprint tested two different models (c30) before 'Race, language and insurance produced none'. Two round 3 judges asked for that clause, and it was not added after scoring.
  • The npj Digital Medicine paper was not read because nature.com answered with a client challenge. The deck rests on UT Southwestern's release and the authors' preprint, and says which is which.
  • Six record items carry an unconfirmed line today. tx-2026-0133, 0161, 0165 and 0173 (uta.edu and unt.edu TLS through the proxy) reach the six day re-verify limit on October 24th.
  • The Bottleneck Scanner's ceiling was not checked. This run holds no D1 access.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it One added line sometimes moved the higher risk patient back, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

In Dallas, researchers added one line.

UT Southwestern's team gave three open source AI models matched pairs of emergency patients. With no stigmatizing detail, all three picked out higher-risk patients at rates well above chance.

Once stigmatizing detail was added, nearly 10% of patients were incorrectly downgraded in some instances. One pair set "established patient with multiple chronic conditions" against "17 visits in the past 12 months."

The records came from Stanford Medicine in California and Beth Israel Deaconess in Massachusetts. Hospitals increasingly explore AI to help prioritize care, the release says.

First author Philip Jarrett says bias varies by model and each tool needs testing against real patient outcomes before use. The release names none of the three models. Which were they?

#UTSouthwestern #EmergencyMedicine #Dallas

The machine changed itself

  • The kit now has a real hospital wristband (patient_wristband): a closed strap with a label patch, a snap, a tail and an alert clip.
    The week's top artwork theme, a primitive model where a kit model belongs (6 decks, 16 rounds), and no. 58's weakest frame, where every judge read the chassis bands as open rings.
  • The kit now has an index card drawer (index_card_drawer) whose card pitch follows its length, so the cards stay inside both walls and a count that can't fit is refused. Divider tabs stand proud and the front has a label holder and a pull.
    No. 58's frame 7 drawer ran off the frame on every render because the chassis model ignored its own length.
  • Slides now carry only the figures their own code reads (scripts/carousel/fig_inject.py), and shipped_check holds every deck after October 23rd to it.
    Writing all of figures.json into every slide made one new figure rewrite nine frames and threw away no. 58's bound art review twice.
  • Proposals for a maintainer, in UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md: the engine needs a way to keep the key off neighbouring objects, and txbench relief casts are too faint under a low key.
    Six decks named a tonal cut that never rendered, no. 58's frame 6 among them, and frames 4 and 8 measured cast fractions of 0.016 and 0.025.
  • For the daily lane: article_check should refuse a number token followed by a percent sign.
    The token already carries the quote's %, so '{{number:c15}}%' printed 'nearly 10%%' in this run's first build, the second time the queue has seen it. It was caught by reading the page and fixed before the shipped rebuild.

Every change is logged in ledger/carousel/upgrades.json.

Notes

The record. Fourteen items re-verified and stamped, tx-2026-0118 moved from open to pending after the CFTC window closed on October 20th, and two items admitted: tx-2026-0228, UT Southwestern's study of AI triage models in Dallas, and tx-2026-0229, the Aggie AI Foundry in Brazos County. The record holds 201 items. Six items carry an unconfirmed line today. tx-2026-0133, 0161, 0165 and 0173 fail TLS on uta.edu and unt.edu through the container's proxy and reach the six day re-verify limit on October 24th if the hosts stay unreachable. The deck. Carousel no. 58 is the UT Southwestern study, told as bone record cards and an ember tape for the added line in the staged lastLight world. Three panel rounds: 6.63, then 6.5 with one hard fail on slide 8 (it overstated the preprint's finding, repaired to the preprint's own words), then 6.948 with no hard fail. It ships at the round cap, 0.75 under round 3's rung, with the art median at 6.4. Weakest frames by the judges: 5, 2, 7, 4 and 8. Slide 8 should say the preprint tested two different models before it says race, language and insurance produced no harmful shift, and that clause is not on the frame. The npj Digital Medicine paper was not read because nature.com challenged the fetcher. Did the run stop for a human. The pre-merge prompt_audit counted 322 of 1,977 calls as waiting, led by Agent and SendMessage spawns at 5 to 28 seconds. The no-stall hook was armed at 05:03:52 UTC, judged the session unattended from its first call with the host's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED at 0, and refused nothing. Nobody answered a dialog, so the waits look like dispatch latency, and that is queued as prompt-audit-counts-agent-latency. This reading was taken before the merge. The machine. The weekly pass ran today because a queued defect reached its second repeat. It lifted a patient wristband and an index card drawer into the kit and added fig_inject so slides carry only the figures they read. Engine and txbench proposals are written up for a maintainer. Not checked. The Bottleneck Scanner's ceiling, because this run holds no D1 access.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
